what: Headline figures from the Commerce Commission's third Annual Grocery Report (2025 report, published 2 June 2026). An annual PDF: there is no feed to fetch, so these are copied by hand and carry the retrieval date. Check again after the next report (expected mid-2027).

report.title: 2025 Annual Grocery Report (Pūrongo ā-Tau mō te Kai)
report.licence: Crown copyright; Commerce Commission material may be reproduced with attribution

regulatedShareNationalPct.label: Regulated grocery retailers (Woolworths NZ, Foodstuffs North Island, Foodstuffs South Island), combined share

regulatedShareAucklandPct.label: Combined share in Auckland, the most competitive market

bannerSharePct.label: Market share by banner
bannerSharePct.note: Figure 5 of the report; Four Square, FreshChoice and SuperValue sit inside the Foodstuffs totals

stores.label: Regulated retailers' store networks
stores.note: Table 1; New World, PAK'nSAVE and Four Square counts are the North Island and South Island co-operatives added together

onlineSharePct.unit: % of regulated retailers' sales revenue, 2025 (7% in 2024)
onlineSharePct.label: Online share of grocery sales

rebatesBillion.unit: NZ$ billion in FY2025, about 26% of combined sales revenue
rebatesBillion.label: Supplier rebates, discounts and payments to the regulated retailers

marketSizeBillion.unit: NZ$ billion a year, year to March 2023
marketSizeBillion.label: Spend at supermarkets and grocery stores

source.name: MBIE, market study into supermarkets, background information

marketSizeBillion.note: Not in the Annual Grocery Report; MBIE's figure, older than the rest of this snapshot

excessProfitMillionPerYear.unit: NZ$ million a year, 2015 to 2019, about $1 million a day
excessProfitMillionPerYear.label: Excess profit the Commission estimated the major retailers earned

source.name: Commerce Commission, market study into the retail grocery sector, final report (March 2022)

excessProfitMillionPerYear.note: From the 2022 market study, not the 2025 Annual Grocery Report
